findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
The following areas are in need of repair:
- Hand sink in kitchen area is pulling from wall. Caulk hand-sink back to wall
- Parts of the wall in between the triple sink and hand-sink are starting peel. Repaint affected areas.

See that areas are repaired. Physical facilities must be smooth and easily cleanable.
findings.citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: The paper towel dispenser at the hand-sink was observed without paper towels. Paper towels were added to the dispenser during the inspection. Ensure that paper towels are available at all times to be sure that hands are getting washed properly.
findings.citation_text: 6-301.12 Hand Drying Provision. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; or (C) A heated-air hand drying device; or (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: The top inner surface of the microwave was observed with accumulated food debris. Discussed and shown to PIC. The microwave was cleaned during the inspection. Ensure that non-food contact surfaces of equipment are cleaned as often as necessary to prevent accumulation and contamination of food.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
The heat puck for measuring the dish machine’s sanitizing temperature was not functioning properly. PIC mentioned that the batteries needed to be replaced. Inspector provided temperature Thermo labels for the facility to use until batteries can be replaced. PIC mentioned that batteries for the puck will be getting replaced soon. Ensure that heat pucks are always functioning in order to properly measure sanitizing temperatures for the dish machine. 

4-302.13: (A) In manual WAREWASHING operations, a TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be provided and readily accessible for frequently measuring the washing and SANITIZING temperatures. (B) In hot water mechanical WAREWASHING operations, an irreversible registering temperature indicator shall be provided and readily accessible for measuring the UTENSIL surface temperature.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Observed the interior cavities of the microwave to be soiled with food debris. Discussed with PIC that the cavities of the microwave should be cleaned as necessary to prevent food contamination. Ensure that the interior of the microwave is cleaned frequently and free of food debris.

4-602.12: (A) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking and baking EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at least every 24 hours. This section does not apply to hot oil cooking and filtering EQUIPMENT if it is cleaned as specified in Subparagraph 4-602.11(D)(6). (B) The cavities and door seals of microwave ovens shall be cleaned at least every 24 hours by using the manufacturer's recommended cleaning procedure.

findings.title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices
findings.citation_text:
5-205.15 Leaks were observed at the plumbing beneath the first and third basins of the kitchen 3 part sink. PIC noted repairs were already made to the plumbing under the middle basin, but parts are needed to replace the pipes under the first basin, which had the worst leak. The third basin had a very slight leak. Pots were observed under all three basins to catch leaking water until repairs are completed. Disposal of wastewater and cleaning of pots were discussed. 
A plumbing system shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.14 Employee exited the restroom and did not wash hands prior to putting on gloves to begin food prep. Employee was asked as to the use of a barrier when exiting the restroom and confirmed a paper towel was not used to touch the door handle. Employee re-washed hands at the kitchen handwashing sink and put on a new pair of gloves upon request of inspector. Ensure hands are properly washed upon re-entering the kitchen after using the restroom and prior to putting on gloves to handle food. Best practice would be to wash hands again in the kitchen after exiting the restroom even if a barrier was used to touch the handle of the door. However, using a paper towel to touch the door handle after properly washing hands in the restroom would negate the need for an additional hand wash in the kitchen as long as no other general surfaces were touched prior to beginning food prep or other tasks. 
Food Employees shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in food preparation including working with exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles. Hands shall also be washed upon entering the kitchen after using the restroom, before putting on gloves to handle food, and after engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.citation_text:
4-302.13 Facility has a heat sanitizing dish machine. Dish temp tester used to verify proper heat sanitization at the surface of dishes was not functioning at the time of inspection. A new battery is needed and will be purchased later today. Inspector’s contract information was provided for staff to send proof of operation once battery has been purchased. Follow-up inspection will not be required if photo of functioning dish temp tester is provided before 2/6/23.
In hot water mechanical warewashing operations, an irreversible registering temperature indicator shall be provided and readily accessible for measuring the utensil surface temperature. Surface temperature at dishes upon completion of final rinse must be at least 160F for proper heat sanitization.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625  Sec. 3.06 Facility is not in compliance with food handler law. One employee had a food handler certification that expired as of 2021, and another employee had a manager certification that expired in September of 2022. Both employees are registered to take a food manager course in February. Ensure proof of manager certification or food handler certification by next routine inspection. 
All food handlers, other than someone who has a food manager certification, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) and (B) Cheese and sauce in the top of the double door cooler was observed at a temperature around 47 and 48 F. Temperature logs of the cooler are taken before prep each day, and it showed the cooler warmed during food prep due to opening and closing of the doors. The PIC was advised to leave the cooler closed as much as possible during food prep to properly cold hold foods. The cooler reached a temperature of 42 after being closed for a few minutes. The cooler was left closed to ensure foods reached the proper cold holding temperature of 41 degreed F. Reference 3-501.16(A)(2) and (B).

findings.title: Thermometers provided & accurate
findings.comment: 4-204-112  (C) A thermometer is not provided in the double door cooler. Cold/Hot holding equipment used for Time/Temperature Control for Safety food shall have at least one thermometer in an easily viewed location. Reference 4-204-112.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Quaternary ammonia sanitizer in spray bottles found below 150 ppm. Staff indicated sanitizer is used to clean tables after lunch in the cafeteria. Staff indicated sanitizer is mixed and stored in bulk containers by janitorial staff and working bottles are filled from bulk. Bulk is estimated to be re-mixed every 2 weeks. Test strips were provided.

->Ensure sanitizer has proper concentrations when using to clean non-food contact surfaces. Check sanitizer concentrations with test strips. Quatnernary ammonia sanitizer must be between 150-400 ppm. Chlorine sanitizer must be between 50-200 ppm. Reference 4-602.13.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114  (P) Chlorine sanitizer at 0 ppm in sanitizer bucket. Provide 100ppm to 200ppm chlorine concentration. Reference 4-501.114.
